work: Enarratio in Epistolam II B. Pauli ad Corinthios
source: Dionysii Cartusiani Opera Omnia, t. XIII (Montreuil)

10.title: EXPOSITIO CAPITULI DECIMI : IPSE AUTEM EGO PAULUS, ETC.
10.title_en: Exposition of the tenth chapter: Now I Paul myself, etc.

paras.t: FACTA exhortatione ad bonos, jam sermo dirigitur ad incorrectos, qui adhuc pseudoapostolis adhæserunt : qui multa vitia imposuerunt Apostolo, de quibus se consequenter excusat, sicut patebit. Ait ergo : Ipse autem ego Paulus obsecro, id est, per sacra rogo, vos, scilicet per mansuetudinem, id est mititatem, quæ iram refrenat, et modestiam, id est moderamen seu discretionem, Christi : qui per Jeremiam ait, Ego quasi agnus mansuetus qui portatur ad victimam; et iterum, Discite a me quia mitis sum et humilis corde ; qui in facie quidem, id est in præsentia vestra, sive exterius, humilis sum inter vos exsistens, quasi blandiens vobis, sicut pseudoapostoli mihi imponunt, absens autem a vobis confido in vobis, id est, fiducialiter, audacter et dure redarguo vos, quia non timeo mihi mala inferri a vobis dum absens sum, quemadmodum præsens. Imposuerunt autem Apostolo quod esset carnalis, quoniam more carnalium, præsens exsistens, dulcis et blandus esset in verbis, quasi timens periculum si durius ageret, absens vero rigidus foret.
paras.en: Having made his exhortation to the good, he now turns his words to the uncorrected, who still clung to the false apostles: these laid many faults to the Apostle's charge, of which he then clears himself, as will appear. He says therefore: [[10:1|Now I Paul, myself beseech|Ipse autem ego Paulus obsecro]], that is, I entreat by holy things, [[10:1|you|vos]], namely [[10:1|by the mildness|per mansuetudinem]], that is, gentleness, which bridles anger, [[10:1|and modesty|et modestiam]], that is, moderation or discretion, [[10:1|of Christ|Christi]]: who says by Jeremias, [[Jer 11:19|I was as a meek lamb, that is carried to be a victim|Ego quasi agnus mansuetus qui portatur ad victimam]]; and again, [[Matt 11:29|learn of me, because I am meek, and humble of heart|Discite a me quia mitis sum et humilis corde]]; [[10:1|who in presence indeed|qui in facie quidem]], that is, in your presence, or outwardly, [[10:1|am lowly among you|humilis sum inter vos]], being as it were one who flatters you, as the false apostles charge against me, [[10:1|but being absent|absens autem]] from you [[10:1|am bold toward you|confido in vobis]], that is, I rebuke you confidently, boldly and harshly, because I do not fear that harm will be done me by you while I am absent, as I would when present. For they charged the Apostle with being carnal, since in the manner of carnal men, when present he was sweet and smooth in his words, as though fearing danger if he dealt more harshly, but when absent he was severe.

paras.t: Rogo autem vos, ne sic sentiatis de me, ne præsens, id est apud vos exsistens, audeam, id est, audacter me habeam, incorrectos durissime increpando, per eam confidentiam, id est fiduciam illam imperterritam, qua existimor ab æmulis audere, id est audacter invehere, in quosdam, id est incorrectos a pseudoapostolis deceptos, quum absens sum, qui incorrecti arbitrantur nos tanquam secundum carnem ambulemus, id est, carnaliter conversari, et in temporalibus finem nos constituere existimant : qui utique errant.
paras.en: [[10:2|But I beseech you|Rogo autem vos]], not to think thus of me, [[10:2|that I may not be bold when I am present|ne præsens audeam]], that is, when among you, be bold, that is, bear myself boldly, rebuking the uncorrected most harshly, [[10:2|with that confidence|per eam confidentiam]], that is, that undaunted assurance, [[10:2|wherewith I am thought to be bold|qua existimor audere]] by my rivals, that is, to inveigh boldly, [[10:2|against some|in quosdam]], that is, the uncorrected deceived by the false apostles, when I am absent; [[10:2|who reckon us as if we walked according to the flesh|qui arbitrantur nos tamquam secundum carnem ambulemus]]: these uncorrected think that we live carnally and set our end in temporal things: and they are certainly mistaken.

paras.t: In carne enim ambulantes, id est in hac corruptibili carne viventes et peregrinantes, non secundum carnem militamus, id est, non carnaliter exercemur ad prælium contra adversarios humanæ salutis. Militia quippe est vita hominis super terram ; sed militia nostra spiritualis est, et triumphum spiritualem intendit. Nam arma militiæ nostræ, quibus prædicando et conversando contra dæmones et perversos homines dimicamus, videlicet virtutes et dona Spiritus Sancti, non carnalia sunt, nec humana virtute adepta, sed potentia Deo, id est Dei virtute efficacia, ad destructionem munitionum, id est virium quibus dæmones et impii homines contra fidei veritatem armantur; consilia impiorum destruentes nostra prædicatione et miraculorum operatione ; et omnem altitudinem, id est præsumptionem ac profunditatem mundanæ et naturalis sapientiæ, extollentem se adversus scientiam Dei, id est theologicæ veritati seu fidei assertionibus contradicentem, destruentes seu reprobantes. Hoc fecit Apostolus Athenis, disputando contra philosophos. Et in captivitatem redigentes, id est, captivantes, et nostræ doctrinæ ac fidei jugo subdentes, omnem intellectum, id est mentem quorumdam de omni genere hominum, in obsequium Christi, id est ad hoc ut Christo deserviant, ejusque auctoritati potius quam humanæ rationi adhæreant. Convertit enim Apostolus quosdam doctos, et quosdam indoctos ; sicque de ceteris generibus hominum quosdam convertit ad Christum : et sic quoque omnium intellectum subjecit fidei præceptisque Christi, quatenus incomprehensibilia credant, et Deo in cunctis obediant.
paras.en: [[10:3|For though we walk in the flesh|In carne enim ambulantes]], that is, living and journeying as pilgrims in this corruptible flesh, [[10:3|we do not war according to the flesh|non secundum carnem militamus]], that is, we are not trained carnally for battle against the adversaries of human salvation. For [[Job 7:1|The life of man upon earth is a warfare|Militia quippe est vita hominis super terram]]; but our warfare is spiritual, and aims at a spiritual triumph. [[10:4|For the weapons of our warfare|Nam arma militiæ nostræ]], with which by preaching and by our manner of life we fight against demons and perverse men, namely the virtues and gifts of the Holy Ghost, [[10:4|are not carnal|non carnalia sunt]], nor gained by human power, [[10:4|but mighty to God|sed potentia Deo]], that is, effective by the power of God, [[10:4|unto the pulling down of fortifications|ad destructionem munitionum]], that is, of the forces with which demons and wicked men arm themselves against the truth of the faith; [[10:4|destroying counsels|consilia destruentes]] of the wicked by our preaching and the working of miracles; [[10:5|And every height|et omnem altitudinem]], that is, the presumption and depth of worldly and natural wisdom, [[10:5|that exalteth itself against the knowledge of God|extollentem se adversus scientiam Dei]], that is, contradicting theological truth or the assertions of the faith, destroying, or confuting. This the Apostle did at Athens, disputing against the philosophers[[Acts 17:16||]]. [[10:5|and bringing into captivity|Et in captivitatem redigentes]], that is, taking captive and subjecting to the yoke of our teaching and faith, [[10:5|every understanding|omnem intellectum]], that is, the minds of some of every kind of men, [[10:5|unto the obedience of Christ|in obsequium Christi]], that is, so that they may serve Christ and adhere to his authority rather than to human reason. For the Apostle converted some learned and some unlearned; and so of the other kinds of men he converted some to Christ: and thus too he subjected the understanding of all to the faith and precepts of Christ, so that they believe things incomprehensible and obey God in all things.

paras.t: Et in promptu habentes, id est, expedite potentes, ulcisci omnem inobedientiam, tradendo excommunicatos et impios Satanæ in interitum carnis, vel, Christum invocando possumus de eis ultionem acquirere, quum impleta fuerit vestra obedientia, id est, perfectam esse noverimus vestram obedientiam. Tunc enim et non ante, decet nos contra rebelles insurgere, quoniam prius confirmandi sunt boni, quam mali torquendi. Ad quod pertinere potest illud Apocalypsis : Nolite nocere terræ et mari, neque arboribus, quoadusque signemus servos Dei nostri in frontibus eorum.
paras.en: [[10:6|And having in readiness|Et in promptu habentes]], that is, being readily able, [[10:6|to revenge all disobedience|ulcisci omnem inobedientiam]], by delivering the excommunicated and wicked to Satan for the destruction of the flesh[[1 Cor 5:5||]]; or, by calling upon Christ we can obtain vengeance on them; [[10:6|when your obedience shall be fulfilled|quum impleta fuerit vestra obedientia]], that is, when we know your obedience to be perfect. For then and not before it befits us to rise against the rebellious, since the good must be strengthened before the wicked are punished. To this may belong that word of the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 7:3|Hurt not the earth nor the sea nor the trees, till we sign the servants of our God in their foreheads|Nolite nocere terræ et mari, neque arboribus, quoadusque signemus servos Dei nostri in frontibus eorum]].

paras.t: Quæ secundum faciem sunt, videte : id est, si prædicta spiritualia quibus ostendi me esse verum Christi apostolum et falsis præferendum, non vobis sufficiunt, quæ secundum faciem sunt, id est, manifeste apparent in illis et in me, videte, id est pensate. Si quis illorum pseudoapostolorum confidit sibi, id est, de propria perfectione præsumit, Christi se esse, id est ad Christum per gratiam se pertinere, hoc cogitet iterum apud se, id est, diligenter consideret atque revolvat, ne se præferat nobis ; quia sicut ipse Christi est, secundum opinionem suam fallacem, ita et nos Christi sumus fideles ministri, secundum veritatem.
paras.en: [[10:7|See the things that are according to outward appearance|Quæ secundum faciem sunt, videte]]: that is, if the spiritual things aforesaid, by which I have shown that I am a true apostle of Christ and to be preferred to the false, are not enough for you, the things that are according to appearance, that is, that plainly appear in them and in me, see, that is, weigh. [[10:7|If any man|Si quis]] of those false apostles [[10:7|trust to himself|confidit sibi]], that is, presumes on his own perfection, [[10:7|that he is Christ's|Christi se esse]], that is, that he belongs to Christ by grace, [[10:7|let him think this again with himself|hoc cogitet iterum apud se]], that is, let him carefully consider and turn it over, lest he prefer himself to us; [[10:7|that as he is Christ's|quia sicut ipse Christi est]], according to his own false opinion, [[10:7|so are we also|ita et nos]] faithful ministers of Christ, according to the truth.

paras.t: Nam et si amplius aliquid gloriatus fuero in Domino de potestate nostra, quam illi de sua gloriari possunt, id est, quamvis illis nostram potestatem prætulero, quam dedit nobis Dominus in ædificationem, et non in destructionem, id est ad hoc ut ea salubriter utamur, non impie abutamur, videlicet ut vos verbis atque exemplis ædificemus in vita spirituali, et non inficiamus nec subvertamus quempiam vestrum ; non erubescam quasi præsumptuose hoc agens, quia sic est. Verumtamen ministri Christi potestate sibi concessa abuti possunt, et sæpius abutuntur, ut patet de malis sacerdotibus, sed non sine grandi peccato.
paras.en: [[10:8|For if also I should boast somewhat more|Nam et si amplius aliquid gloriatus fuero]] in the Lord [[10:8|of our power|de potestate nostra]] than they can glory of theirs, that is, even though I should prefer our power to theirs, [[10:8|which the Lord hath given us unto edification|quam dedit nobis Dominus in ædificationem]], and not for destruction, that is, so that we may use it to salvation, not wickedly abuse it, namely that we may build you up in the spiritual life by words and examples, and not infect or overthrow any of you; [[10:8|I should not be ashamed|non erubescam]], as though doing this presumptuously, because it is so. Yet the ministers of Christ can abuse the power granted them, and quite often do, as is plain of bad priests, but not without grave sin.

paras.t: Denique, ne isti erronei æstimarent Apostolum non esse facturum quum præsens adesset, quod absens minabatur, dicendo se potentem et promptum ulcisci omnem inobedientiam : ne igitur ita sentirent, adjunxit : Ut autem non existimer ab incorrectis et falsis, tanquam terrere vos per epistolas, id est in epistolis meis ad vos missis verba minatoria miscere, quæ non audebo præsens implere (nam hoc mihi imponunt) ; quoniam quidem epistolæ meæ, inquiunt illi detractores, graves sunt et fortes, id est minaces, et intellectu difficiles, atque verbosæ, præsentia autem corporis infirma, id est, nos ipsi corporaliter præsentes, impotentes et timidi sumus, non audentes exercere rigorem, sed adulantes, et sermo noster contemptibilis, id est non rhetoricus, nec humanis argumentis firmatus, sed simplex et nudus, nil probans ; hoc cogitet qui ejusmodi est, id est qui talia nobis imponit, quia quales sumus verbo per epistolas, id est in epistolis, dum sumus absentes, tales erimus et præsentes, in facto, id est, opere exsequemur quæcumque minamur, et nos facturos prædicimus in epistolis vobis transmissis.
paras.en: Further, lest these erring men should think that the Apostle would not do when present what he threatened when absent, saying that he was able and ready to revenge all disobedience: lest, then, they should think so, he added: [[10:9|But that I may not be thought|Ut autem non existimer]] by the uncorrected and false, [[10:9|as it were to terrify you by epistles|tanquam terrere vos per epistolas]], that is, to mingle threatening words in my letters sent to you, which I will not dare to fulfil when present (for this they charge against me); [[10:10|For his epistles indeed|quoniam quidem epistolæ]] (my epistles), [[10:10|say they|inquiunt]], those detractors, [[10:10|are weighty and strong|graves sunt et fortes]], that is, threatening, and hard to understand, and wordy, [[10:10|but his bodily presence is weak|præsentia autem corporis infirma]], that is, we ourselves, bodily present, are powerless and timid, not daring to use severity, but flattering, [[10:10|and his speech contemptible|et sermo contemptibilis]] (our speech), that is, not rhetorical, nor supported by human arguments, but simple and bare, proving nothing; [[10:11|Let such a one think this|hoc cogitet qui ejusmodi est]], that is, he who lays such things to our charge, [[10:11|that such as we are in word by epistles|quia quales sumus verbo per epistolas]], that is, in epistles, while we are [[10:11|when absent|absentes]], [[10:11|such also we will be indeed when present|tales erimus et præsentes, in facto]], that is, we will carry out in deed whatever we threaten and foretell that we will do in the epistles sent to you.

paras.t: Non enim audemus salva conscientia, inserere, id est connumerare, aut comparare, id est vere pares asserere, nos, quibusdam qui semetipsos commendant ob propriam laudem et aliorum deceptionem, videlicet ambitiosis et pseudoapostolis, qui potestatem sibi usurpant, et delinquentium vitia palpant. Si enim diceremus nos eis pares aut similes, mentiremur. Sed nos ipsi in nobis, id est in consideratione et examine mentis nostræ, sumus nosmetipsos metientes seu mensurantes, id est, nos ipsos diligenter discutimus, gratiamque nobis collatam perpendimus, ne præfixos nobis terminos transgrediamur, et plus justo nos ipsos jactemus, et sumus comparantes nosmetipsos nobis, id est, moderate et sobrie de nobis sentimus, propriamque mensuram pensamus.
paras.en: [[10:12|For we dare not match|Non enim audemus inserere]] with a safe conscience, that is, number ourselves among, [[10:12|or compare ourselves with some|aut comparare nos quibusdam]], that is, truly declare ourselves equal, [[10:12|that commend themselves|qui seipsos commendant]] for their own praise and the deceiving of others, namely the ambitious and the false apostles, who usurp power to themselves and stroke [that is, flatter and pass over] the vices of offenders. For if we said we were equal or like to them, we should lie. [[10:12|but we measure ourselves by ourselves|sed ipsi in nobis nosmetipsos metientes]], that is, in the consideration and examination of our mind we measure ourselves, that is, we examine ourselves carefully and weigh the grace bestowed on us, lest we pass the bounds set for us and boast of ourselves more than is just; [[10:12|and compare ourselves with ourselves|et comparantes nosmetipsos nobis]], that is, we think of ourselves with moderation and sobriety, and weigh our own measure.

paras.t: Nos autem non in immensum gloriabimur, id est, ultra terminum nobis divinitus præstitutum nihil præsumimus, sed gloriamur, et gloriando exercemus nostræ prædicationis officium, secundum mensuram regulæ, id est secundum extensionem ordinationis divinæ, quæ omnium rerum prima regula est; quam mensuram seu extensionem mensus est nobis Deus, id est, perambulandam præfixit sapientia Dei : cujus nutu missi sunt singuli Apostolorum ad certas determinatasque gentes, de quarum conversione gloriarentur in Domino. Ideo subditur : mensuram pertingendi usque ad vos : quia ex divina revelatione perrexit Apostolus Corinthum.
paras.en: [[10:13|But we will not glory beyond our measure|Nos autem non in immensum gloriabimur]], that is, we presume nothing beyond the bound divinely set for us; [[10:13|but|sed]] we glory, and in glorying exercise the office of our preaching, [[10:13|according to the measure of the rule|secundum mensuram regulæ]], that is, according to the extent of the divine ordinance, which is the first rule of all things; [[10:13|which God hath measured to us|qua mensus est nobis Deus]], which measure or extent the wisdom of God has appointed for us to travel through: by whose will each of the Apostles was sent to certain fixed nations, of whose conversion they might glory in the Lord. Therefore it is added: [[10:13|a measure to reach even unto you|mensuram pertingendi usque ad vos]]: for by divine revelation the Apostle went to Corinth.

paras.t: Non enim quasi non pertingentes ad vos, ad quorum conversionem destinati sumus, superextendimus nos, id est, ultra præscriptum a Deo terminum non tendimus. Usque ad vos enim pervenimus in Evangelio Christi, id est in prædicatione evangelica. Non tamen dumtaxat usque ad Corinthum venit, quippe qui ad Illyricum mare per circuitum Evangelium Christi replevit.
paras.en: [[10:14|For we stretch not ourselves beyond our measure, as if we reached not unto you|Non enim quasi non pertingentes ad vos, superextendimus nos]], to whose conversion we were appointed: that is, we do not reach beyond the bound prescribed by God. [[10:14|For we are come as far as to you in the Gospel of Christ|Usque ad vos enim pervenimus in Evangelio Christi]], that is, in the preaching of the gospel. Yet he did not come only as far as Corinth, since round about as far as the Illyrian sea he filled all with the Gospel of Christ[[Rom 15:19||]].

paras.t: Non in immensum, id est sine debito moderamine, gloriantes in alienis laboribus, id est in prædicatione et conversione aliorum, quasi illos labores nobis attribuamus, vel de conversis per alios principaliter gloriemur ; sed gloriamur de nostro labore in vestri conversione ; spem autem habentes crescentis fidei vestræ, id est, profectum sumus sperantes de fide vestra crescente et proficiente de uno virtuoso actu in alium. Quis autem sit iste profectus speratus (qui dicitur spes, sumendo spem pro bono sperato), subjungitur : in vobis magnificari, id est in cordibus vestris tales esse seu cognosci, quales veraciter sumus, ne posthac vilipendamur a vobis ; vel, In vobis, id est per vos magnificari apud alios, quibus ex vestri conversione ac perfectione innotescit nos esse veros Dei apostolos : magnificari autem secundum regulam nostram, id est secundum mensuram, proportionem seu modum gratiæ nobis collatæ, ne quis nos altiores putet quam sumus; in abundantia,
paras.en: [[10:15|Not glorying beyond measure|Non in immensum]], that is, without due moderation, [[10:15|in other men's labours|gloriantes in alienis laboribus]], that is, in the preaching and conversion of others, as if we attributed those labours to ourselves, or gloried chiefly of those converted by others; but we glory of our own labour in your conversion; [[10:15|but having hope of your increasing faith|spem autem habentes crescentis fidei vestræ]], that is, hoping for progress from your faith growing and advancing from one virtuous act to another. And what this hoped-for progress is (which is called hope, taking hope for the good hoped for), is added: [[10:15|to be magnified in you|in vobis magnificari]], that is, in your hearts to be, or to be known as, such as we truly are, lest hereafter we be despised by you; or, In you, that is, through you to be magnified among others, to whom it becomes known from your conversion and perfection that we are true apostles of God: to be magnified, moreover, [[10:15|according to our rule|secundum regulam nostram]], that is, according to the measure, proportion or manner of the grace bestowed on us, lest anyone think us higher than we are; [[10:15|abundantly|in abundantia]],

paras.t: id est in copiosa ac fervida promptitudine animi, parati sumus etiam in illa quæ ultra vos sunt loca evangelizare, id est gentibus valde distantibus prædicare, non in aliena regula, id est mensura seu plebe aliis commissa, videlicet in his quæ præparata sunt, id est per prædicationem aliorum ad fidem conversa, gloriari inaniter. Non enim in illis gloriabatur Apostolus, sicut nunc dictum est, sed de iis qui suæ sorti contigerant. Unde Romanis dixit : Sic autem prædicavi Evangelium hoc, non ubi nominatus est Christus, ne super alienum fundamentum ædificarem.
paras.en: that is, in a plentiful and fervent readiness of mind, we are prepared [[10:16|Yea, unto those places that are beyond you|etiam in illa quæ ultra vos sunt]], places, [[10:16|to preach the gospel|evangelizare]], that is, to preach to nations very far off; [[10:16|not to glory in another man's rule|non in aliena regula in iis quæ præparata sunt gloriari]], that is, in a measure or people committed to others, namely [[10:16|in those things that are made ready|in iis quæ præparata sunt]], that is, converted to the faith by the preaching of others, to glory vainly. For the Apostle did not glory in these, as has just been said, but of those who had fallen to his own lot. Hence he said to the Romans: [[Rom 15:20|so preached this gospel, not where Christ was named, lest I should build upon another man a foundation|Sic autem prædicavi Evangelium hoc, non ubi nominatus est Christus, ne super alienum fundamentum ædificarem]].

paras.t: Qui autem gloriatur, in Domino, id est secundum doctrinam et voluntatem Domini, glorietur, omnia bona ad Deum referendo finaliter. Vel, In Domino, id est in contemplatione ac dilectione divina : imo in omni actu virtuoso lætandum est. Hoc modo gloriabatur Virgo benedicta, dicendo : Exsultavit spiritus meus in Deo salutari meo. Et Habacuc : Ego, inquit, in Domino gaudebo, et exsultabo in Deo Jesu meo. Debemus quoque gloriari in Domino, congratulando totis præcordiis divinæ beatitudini ac perfectioni.
paras.en: [[10:17|But he that glorieth|Qui autem gloriatur]], [[10:17|in the Lord|in Domino]][[1 Cor 1:31||]][[Jer 9:23||]][[Jer 9:24||]], that is, according to the teaching and will of the Lord, [[10:17|let him glory|glorietur]], referring all goods to God as their end. Or, In the Lord, that is, in divine contemplation and love: indeed one must rejoice in every virtuous act. In this way the blessed Virgin gloried, saying: [[Luke 1:47|my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour|spiritus meus in Deo salutari meo]]. And Habacuc: [[Hab 3:18|I will rejoice in the Lord: and I will joy in God my Jesus|Ego … in Domino gaudebo … in Deo Jesu meo]]. We ought also to glory in the Lord by rejoicing with all our heart in the divine beatitude and perfection.

paras.t: Non enim qui se ipsum commendat ob propriam laudem, ille probatus justus vel approbatus est coram Deo et discretis personis, sed reprobatus : quoniam Salomon ait, Laudet te alienus, et non os tuum; sed probatus est quem Deus commendat, id est, laude dignum judicat, seu commendabilem facit per virtutes et signa.
paras.en: [[10:18|For not he who commendeth himself|Non enim qui seipsum commendat]] for his own praise, [[10:18|is approved|ille probatus est]] as just, or approved, before God and discerning persons, but rather reproved: for Solomon says, [[Prov 27:2|Let another praise thee, and not thy own mouth|Laudet te alienus, et non os tuum]]; [[10:18|but he|sed]] is approved [[10:18|whom God commendeth|quem Deus commendat]], that is, judges worthy of praise, or makes commendable by virtues and signs.

11.title: ELUCIDATIO CAPITULI UNDECIMI : UTINAM SUSTINERETIS MODICUM QUID INSIPIENTIÆ MEÆ.
11.title_en: Elucidation of the eleventh chapter: Would to God you could bear with some little of my folly

paras.t: Completa excusatione Apostoli, qua a se excusavit de malis sibi a pseudoapostolis impositis, nunc invehitur contra illos. Et primo petit se patienter audiri a suis. Utinam sustineretis modicum quid insipientiæ meæ, id est, utinam æquanimiter audiretis paululum verba mea, quibus laudo me ipsum : quod esse videtur insipientis, et ab aliquibus fatuum reputatur, quum dicat Scriptura, Laudet te alienus, et non os tuum. Quocirca sciendum, quod moralia, quum versentur circa particularia, mutabilia sunt, atque mutanda secundum diversitatem locorum, causarum, temporum et personarum. Idcirco de eis tam certæ regulæ dari non possunt, quin vicissim patiantur instantiam propter rationabilem causam : quod viri eruditi attendunt, non autem indocti. Unde quum aliquid fit a justo vel sapiente, quod contrariari videtur verbis regularum moralium, quamvis intentioni earum non repugnet, indiscreti ac stolidi judicant illud illicitum. Quum ergo Scriptura prohibeat laudare se ipsum, insipientiæ est semper secundum opinionem stultorum, ut quisquam laudet se ipsum. Ideo dicit Apostolus, se optare ut sustineant modicum insipientiæ suæ secundum æstimationem indiscretorum : quod tamen, secundum veritatem, erat magnum quid sapientiæ. Salomonis enim verbum intelligendum est, quando occultatio propriæ laudis non vergit in præjudicium veritatis, nec in detrimentum salutis proximorum, nec in honoris divini dispendium : et ob has causas Paulus commendavit se ipsum. Simili modo solvitur quod Apostolus in suis epistolis toties suos laudat discipulos, quum tamen in Ecclesiastico scriptum sit : Ante mortem ne laudes hominem quemquam.
paras.en: The Apostle's excuse being completed, by which he cleared himself of the evils laid upon him by the false apostles, he now inveighs against them. And first he asks to be heard patiently by his own. [[11:1|Would to God you could bear with some little of my folly!|Utinam sustineretis modicum quid insipientiæ meæ]], that is, would that you would hear with equanimity a few words of mine, in which I praise myself: which seems to belong to a fool, and is reckoned foolish by some, since Scripture says: [[Prov 27:2|Let another praise thee, and not thy own mouth|Laudet te alienus, et non os tuum]]. Wherefore it must be known that moral matters, since they concern particulars, are changeable, and are to be changed according to the diversity of places, causes, times and persons. Therefore such certain rules cannot be given about them that they do not in turn admit exceptions for a reasonable cause: which learned men attend to, but not the unlearned. Hence when something is done by a just or wise man which seems to contradict the words of moral rules, though it does not oppose their intention, the indiscreet and stolid judge it unlawful. Since then Scripture forbids praising oneself, it is always folly in the opinion of fools for anyone to praise himself. Therefore the Apostle says he wishes they would bear a little of his folly according to the estimate of the indiscreet: which nevertheless, in truth, was a great piece of wisdom. For Solomon's word is to be understood of when the concealment of one's own praise does not turn to the prejudice of truth, nor to the detriment of the salvation of neighbours, nor to the loss of God's honour: and for these causes Paul commended himself. In like manner is resolved the fact that the Apostle in his epistles so often praises his disciples, though in Ecclesiasticus it is written: [[Ecclus 11:30|Praise not any man before death|Ante mortem ne laudes hominem]].

paras.t: Sed et supportate me, id est, patienter auscultate quæ dico, et ferte me sicut decet prælatum supportari a subditis suis. Et merito me supportare debetis : Æmulor enim vos, id est, ardenter diligo, non qualitercumque, seu carnali affectione, sed Dei æmulatione, id est sincero ac deiformi amore, videlicet ad hunc finem ad quem vos amat Deus, ut consequamini vitam æternam. — Denique, Æmulari, multis modis accipitur : Primo, pro indignatione, juxta illud Ezechielis : Erat idolum zeli ad provocandum æmulationem. Secundo, pro rancore, ut ad Romanos Paulus : Non in contentione et æmulatione. Tertio, pro desiderio boni nondum adepti, sicut dictum est supra : Æmulamini charismata meliora. Quarto, pro dilectione, ut ibi : Fortis est ut mors dilectio, dura sicut inferus æmulatio. Quinto, pro inordinato amore, ut est illud Apostoli : Æmulantur vos non bene. Sexto, pro imitatione, juxta illud : Bonum æmulamini in bono semper.
paras.en: [[11:1|But do bear with me|Sed et supportare me]], that is, listen patiently to what I say, and bear with me as it befits a prelate to be borne with by his subjects. And rightly ought you to bear with me: [[11:2|For I am jealous of you|æmulor enim vos]], that is, I love you ardently, not in any fashion whatever, or with carnal affection, but [[11:2|with the jealousy of God|Dei æmulatione]], that is, with a sincere and godlike love, namely to that end for which God loves you, that you may attain eternal life. — Further, *to be jealous* [æmulari] is taken in many ways. First, for indignation, as in Ezechiel: [[Ezech 8:3|where was set the idol of jealousy to provoke to jealousy|idolum zeli ad provocandum æmulationem]]. Secondly, for rancour, as Paul to the Romans: [[Rom 13:13|not in contention and envy|Non in contentione et æmulatione]]. Thirdly, for desire of a good not yet obtained, as was said above: [[1 Cor 12:31|be zealous for the better gifts|Æmulamini charismata meliora]]. Fourthly, for love, as there: [[Cant 8:6|love is strong as death, jealousy as hard as hell|Fortis est ut mors dilectio, dura sicut inferus æmulatio]]. Fifthly, for disordered love, as that of the Apostle: [[Gal 4:17|They are zealous in your regard not well|Æmulantur vos non bene]]. Sixthly, for imitation, as in that: [[Gal 4:18|be zealous for that which is good in a good thing always|Bonum æmulamini in bono semper]].

paras.t: Quod autem æmuler vos, patet : Despondi enim annulo fidei, id est, spirituali matrimonio junxi, vos omnes fideles, uni viro, videlicet Christo, virginem castam exhibere Christo, id est ad hoc ut exhibeam vos Christo sponsam ac virginem illibatam. Omnes enim fideles caritate connexi, sunt una sponsa Christi unaque virgo spiritualiter, propter integræ fidei unitatem. Carnis namque virginitas, est integritas corporis a contagione carnali; virginitas cordis, est fides incorrupta. Unde apud Osee Dominus loquitur : Sponsabo te mihi in fide. Ideo singulariter dixit, Virginem, propter unitatem catholicæ fidei, solidæ spei, atque amoris divini. Hujus conjunctionis internæ ac matrimonialis inter Christum et Ecclesiam paranymphus erat Apostolus, tanquam Sponsi secretarius et amicus.
paras.en: That I am jealous of you is plain: [[11:2|For I have espoused|Despondi enim]] with the ring of faith, that is, joined in spiritual marriage, [[11:2|you|vos]] all the faithful, [[11:2|to one husband|uni viro]], namely Christ, [[11:2|that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ|virginem castam exhibere Christo]], that is, to this end, that I may present you to Christ as a bride and an unspotted virgin. For all the faithful joined by charity are spiritually one bride of Christ and one virgin, because of the unity of entire faith. For virginity of the flesh is the integrity of the body from carnal contagion; virginity of the heart is uncorrupted faith. Hence in Osee the Lord speaks: [[Osee 2:20|I will espouse thee to me in faith|Sponsabo te mihi in fide]]. Therefore he said *virgin* in the singular, because of the unity of the Catholic faith, of firm hope, and of divine love. Of this inward and matrimonial union between Christ and the Church the Apostle was the paranymph [that is, the friend of the bridegroom who arranges the marriage], as the Bridegroom's confidant and friend.

paras.t: Consequenter præmonet Apostolus Corinthios contra futura pericula, scilicet ne recidivent, vel tentationibus superentur. Timeo autem, ne sicut serpens, id est diabolus : de quo in Isaia legitur, Visitabit Dominus super Leviathan serpentem tortuosum ; Evam in paradiso seduxit astutia, id est calliditate sua, dicens : Nequaquam moriemini, sed eritis sicut dii ; ita corrumpantur sensus vestri, id est, intellectus vestri mendaciter informentur a pseudodoctoribus et pestiferis, et excidant a simplicitate, id est a pura fide et simplici veritate, quæ est in Christo, sicut in causa atque magistro ; vel, Est in Christo, quoniam est secundum beneplacitum ejus, et complacet ei. Timeo ergo ne decipiamini a falsis doctoribus, sed non debetis eos advertere : Nam si is fallax qui venit, id est, vos accedit gratia informandi, alium Christum, id est excellentiorem salvatorem, prædicat vobis quem non prædicavimus : quod esse non potest, quum Christum dicamus Deum verum; aut alium spiritum meliorem accipitis per prædicationem falsam, quem non accepistis ex prædicatione nostra : quod esse non potest, quia per nostram prædicationem vobis est datus Spiritus Sanctus verus Deus ; aut aliud, id est salubrius, evangelium recipitis ab illo fallaci, quod non recepistis : quod esse non valet ; recte pateremini, id est, tunc merito sustineretis doctrinam illorum fallacium. Sed ita non est :
paras.en: Next the Apostle forewarns the Corinthians against future dangers, namely lest they relapse or be overcome by temptations. [[11:3|But I fear lest, as the serpent|Timeo autem ne sicut serpens]], that is, the devil, of whom we read in Isaias: [[Is 27:1|the Lord with his hard, and great, and strong sword shall visit leviathan the bar serpent|Visitabit Dominus super Leviathan serpentem tortuosum]]; [[11:3|seduced Eve|Hevam seduxit]] in paradise [[11:3|by his subtilty|astutia sua]], that is, his cunning, saying: [[Gen 3:4|No, you shall not die|Nequaquam moriemini]], [[Gen 3:5|you shall be as Gods|eritis sicut dii]]; [[11:3|so your minds should be corrupted|ita corrumpantur sensus vestri]], that is, your understandings be falsely informed by pestilent false teachers, [[11:3|and fall from the simplicity|et excidant a simplicitate]], that is, from pure faith and simple truth, [[11:3|that is in Christ|quæ est in Christo]], as in its cause and master; or, *is in Christ*, because it is according to His good pleasure and is pleasing to Him. I fear then lest you be deceived by false teachers; but you ought not to heed them: [[11:4|For if he that cometh|Nam si is qui venit]], deceitful, that is, comes to you on the pretext of instructing you, [[11:4|preacheth another Christ|alium Christum prædicat]], that is, a more excellent saviour, to you, [[11:4|whom we have not preached|quem non prædicavimus]]: which cannot be, since we call Christ true God; [[11:4|or if you receive another Spirit|aut alium spiritum accipitis]], a better one, through false preaching, [[11:4|whom you have not received|quem non accepistis]] from our preaching: which cannot be, since through our preaching the Holy Ghost, true God, was given you; [[11:4|or another gospel|aut aliud Evangelium]], that is, a more salutary one, received from that deceiver, [[11:4|which you have not received|quod non recepistis]]: which cannot be; [[11:4|you might well bear with him|recte pateremini]], that is, then you would rightly bear the doctrine of those deceivers. But it is not so:

paras.t: Existimo enim nihil me minus fecisse, docendo, miracula operando, gratiam Spiritus Sancti vobis impetrando, a magnis, id est veris Apostolis : et per consequens præferendi mihi non sunt pseudoapostoli. Nam et si ego imperitus sum sermone, id est ignarus humanæ eloquentiæ, præsertim in lingua peregrina; sed non scientia imperitus sum, quum sim in divinis Scripturis eruditus, non solum humana instructione ad pedes Gamalielis, sed multo copiosius ex illuminatione divina in raptu meo usque ad tertium cœlum. Sed videtur Apostolus agere contra id quod ipse alios docuit, dicens : Qui se existimat aliquid scire, nondum scit quemadmodum oporteat eum scire. Et Salomon ait : Vidisti hominem sapientem sibi videri? magis illo spem stultus habebit. Et respondendum, quod hæc atque similia ideo dicuntur, quia non debet aliquis sapiens esse in oculis propriis, adscribendo sibi quod habet, sed solum in Domino. In omnibus autem verbis et factis manifestatus sum vobis, id est, experimento didicistis, qualis sim, et quantam a Domino sortitus sim gratiam, in docendo, conversando, et signa agendo.
paras.en: [[11:5|For I suppose that I have done nothing less|Existimo enim nihil me minus fecisse]], in teaching, working miracles, obtaining for you the grace of the Holy Ghost, [[11:5|than the great apostles|a magnis Apostolis]], that is, the true Apostles: and consequently the false apostles are not to be preferred to me. [[11:6|For although I be rude in speech|Nam etsi imperitus sermone]], that is, unskilled in human eloquence, especially in a foreign tongue, [[11:6|yet not in knowledge|sed non scientia]] am I unskilled, since I am learned in the divine Scriptures, not only by human instruction at the feet of Gamaliel[[Acts 22:3||]], but far more abundantly by divine illumination in my rapture to the third heaven[[2 Cor 12:2||]]. But the Apostle seems to act against what he himself taught others, saying: [[1 Cor 8:2|if any man think that he knoweth any thing, he hath not yet known as he ought to know|Qui se existimat aliquid scire, nondum scit quemadmodum oporteat eum scire]]. And Solomon says: [[Prov 26:12|Hast thou seen a man wise in his own conceit? there shall be more hope of a fool than of him|Vidisti hominem sapientem sibi videri? magis illo spem stultus habebit]]. And the answer is that these and similar things are said because no one ought to be wise in his own eyes, ascribing to himself what he has, but only in the Lord. [[11:6|but in all things we have been made manifest to you|in omnibus autem manifestati sumus vobis]] in words and deeds, that is, you have learned by experience what I am, and how great a grace I have received from the Lord, in teaching, in conversation, and in working signs.

paras.t: Deinde ostendit Apostolus, quod propter suam humilitatem non debeat vilipendi. Aut numquid peccatum feci, me ipsum humilians, id est, inferioribus me conformans, propriis manibus laborando, et non tanquam prælatus de bonis vestris vivendo, ut vos exaltemini, id est, profectum sumatis in gratia, ædificati meæ humilitatis ac agilitatis exemplo? Humiliavi autem me, quoniam gratis, id est sine acceptione temporalis commodi, Evangelium Dei evangelizavi vobis. Alias autem Ecclesias exspoliavi accipiens stipendium, id est, a ceteris fidelium cœtibus multa accepi stipendia vitæ, ad ministerium vestrum, id est ad hoc ut vobis liberius prædicare possem. Et quum essem apud vos, et egerem victu, nulli vestrum onerosus fui, aliquid exigendo vel recipiendo a vobis. Nam quod mihi deerat pro sustentatione vitæ, consumptis his quæ ab aliis Ecclesiis cepi, suppleverunt, id est, mihi dederunt, fratres qui venerunt ad me a Macedonia: a quibus tanquam a bene correctis aliquid accepi, præsertim ne tristarentur et fructu eleemosynæ privarentur, si nihil ab eis sumpsissem. Et in omnibus diebus atque negotiis, sine onere me vobis servavi, a receptione stipendiorum vestrorum seu sumptuum abstinendo, et servabo in posterum.
paras.en: Then the Apostle shows that he ought not to be despised for his humility. [[11:7|Or did I commit a fault, humbling myself|Aut numquid peccatum feci, meipsum humilians]], that is, conforming myself to the lowly, labouring with my own hands[[1 Cor 4:12||]], and not living on your goods as a prelate, [[11:7|that you might be exalted|ut vos exaltemini]], that is, might make progress in grace, edified by the example of my humility and diligence? Now I humbled myself [[11:7|because I preached unto you the Gospel of God freely?|quoniam gratis Evangelium Dei evangelizavi vobis]], that is, without receiving temporal advantage. [[11:8|I have taken from other churches, receiving wages|Alias ecclesias expoliavi, accipiens stipendium]] [literally, “I despoiled other churches”], that is, from the other assemblies of the faithful I received much support for life, [[11:8|for your ministry|ad ministerium vestrum]], that is, so that I might preach to you more freely. [[11:9|And, when I was present with you and wanted|Et cum essem apud vos, et egerem]] food, [[11:9|I was chargeable to no man|nulli onerosus fui]] of you, by demanding or receiving anything from you. [[11:9|for that which was wanting to me|nam quod mihi deerat]] for the sustenance of life, when what I had taken from other churches was spent, [[11:9|the brethren supplied who came from Macedonia|suppleverunt fratres, qui venerunt a Macedonia]], that is, gave me: from whom, as being well amended, I accepted something, especially lest they should be grieved and deprived of the fruit of almsgiving had I taken nothing from them. [[11:9|And in all things I have kept myself from being burthensome to you|et in omnibus sine onere me vobis servavi]] days and affairs, abstaining from receiving your wages or expenses, [[11:9|and so I will keep myself|et servabo]] in future.

paras.t: Est veritas Christi in me, id est, per veritatem Christi in me exsistentem hoc assero, quoniam hæc gloria, id est ista perfectio et bona gloriatio, scilicet quod prædicavi vobis sine gravamine vestro, non infringetur, id est, non tolletur neque deficiet, in me in regionibus, id est Ecclesiis, Achaiæ : cujus metropolis est Corinthus. Quare? id est, cur hoc ago et agam? an ideo quia non diligo vos? Deus scit quod non facio ideo. Unde constat quod interdum ad dilectionem pertineat, aliquid ab alio capere; ad odium vero, nil velle recipere. Quod autem facio, et faciam, servando me vobis sine onere, ideo facio, ut amputem occasionem eorum qui volunt occasionem, id est, studium pseudoapostolorum impediam, qui quærunt occasionem aliquid acquirendi a vobis meo exemplo. Unde si viderent me vestris stipendiis sustentari, ipsi audaciam sumerent multa exigendi a vobis. Amputo ergo occasionem eorum, ut in quo gloriantur, id est in apostolatu, de quo se inaniter jactant, inveniantur sicut et nos, id est similes nobis sint, nil accipiendo a vobis, sicut et nos nihil accipimus. Quod autem inaniter gloriantur de suo officio, patet :
paras.en: [[11:10|The truth of Christ is in me|Est veritas Christi in me]], that is, by the truth of Christ existing in me I assert this, [[11:10|that this glorying|quoniam hæc gloriatio]], that is, this perfection and good boasting, namely that I preached to you without burdening you, [[11:10|shall not be broken off|non infringetur]], that is, shall not be taken away nor fail, [[11:10|in me in the regions of Achaia|in me in regionibus Achaiæ]], that is, the churches of Achaia, whose metropolis is Corinth. [[11:11|Wherefore?|Quare?]] that is, why do I do and will I do this? Is it [[11:11|Because I love you not? God knoweth it|quia non diligo vos? Deus scit]], that I do not do it for that reason. Hence it is clear that sometimes it belongs to love to take something from another, and to hatred to be unwilling to receive anything. [[11:12|But what I do, that I will do|Quod autem facio, et faciam]], keeping myself from burdening you, I do for this, [[11:12|that I may cut off the occasion from them that desire occasion|ut amputem occasionem eorum qui volunt occasionem]], that is, that I may hinder the zeal of the false apostles, who seek occasion of getting something from you by my example. For if they saw me supported by your wages, they would take boldness to exact much from you. I cut off their occasion, then, [[11:12|that wherein they glory|ut in quo gloriantur]], that is, in the apostleship of which they vainly boast, [[11:12|they may be found even as we|inveniantur sicut et nos]], that is, be like us, taking nothing from you, as we too take nothing. That they glory vainly in their office is plain:

paras.t: Nam ejusmodi pseudoapostoli, sunt operarii subdoli, id est fallaces ministri, transfigurantes se sunt in Apostolos Christi, id est, speciem religionis assumunt, sanctitatem simulant, et per exteriorem apparentiam ostentant se ac si essent veri Apostoli. Et non mirum est hoc : ipse enim Satanas princeps illorum, transfigurat se in angelum lucis, id est, in similitudine Christi Angeli magni consilii, seu alterius cujuscumque angelici spiritus, se ostendit, quantum ad formam assumptam. Multa quoque vera et bona suggerit, quatenus credatur missus a Deo, et fallat. Ideo per alium Apostolum dicitur : Nolite omni spiritui credere, sed probate spiritus, si ex Deo sunt. Non est ergo magnum, id est multum mirandum, si ministri ejus, id est homines seductores, transfigurentur, id est, sanctitatis speciem exterius induant, velut sint ministri justitiæ. Quorum ministrorum, tam Christi quam Satanæ, finis, id est retributio finalis, erit secundum opera ipsorum.
paras.en: [[11:13|For such false apostles are deceitful workmen|Nam ejusmodi pseudoapostoli sunt operarii subdoli]], that is, false ministers, [[11:13|transforming themselves into the apostles of Christ|transfigurantes se in apostolos Christi]], that is, they put on the appearance of religion, feign holiness, and by outward show display themselves as though they were true Apostles. [[11:14|And no wonder|Et non mirum]] is this: [[11:14|for Satan himself|ipse enim Satanas]], their prince, [[11:14|transformeth himself into an angel of light|transfigurat se in angelum lucis]], that is, shows himself, as to the form assumed, in the likeness of Christ, the Angel of great counsel[[Is 9:6||]] [the margin gives Is. ix, 6 “according to the Septuagint”], or of any other angelic spirit. He also suggests many true and good things, so that he may be believed sent by God, and may deceive. Therefore it is said by another Apostle: [[1 John 4:1|believe not every spirit, but try the spirits if they be of God|Nolite omni spiritui credere, sed probate spiritus, si ex Deo sunt]]. [[11:15|Therefore it is no great thing|Non est ergo magnum]], that is, much to be wondered at, [[11:15|if his ministers|si ministri ejus]], that is, seducing men, [[11:15|be transformed|transfigurentur]], that is, outwardly put on the appearance of holiness, [[11:15|as the ministers of justice|velut ministri justitiæ]]. [[11:15|whose|quorum]] ministers, both of Christ and of Satan, [[11:15|end|finis]], that is, final retribution, [[11:15|shall be according to their works|erit secundum opera ipsorum]].

paras.t: Iterum dico quod dixi superius, scilicet, Supportate me, et, Utinam sustineretis modicum quid insipientiæ meæ; ne quis me putet insipientem, dum de spiritualibus gratiis mihi collatis glorior, quum non inaniter glorier, sed in Domino, ad ædificationem proximorum. Alioqui, id est, si non sustinetis me in spiritualibus gloriantem, velut insipientem accipite me gloriantem in carnalibus, secundum modum dicendum : quæ gloriatio videtur magis insipiens, quam illa quæ de spiritualibus est, quamvis nulla earum in me fuit vana ac stulta, sed propter efficacem causam assumpta. Sic ergo accipite me, ut et ego modicum quid glorier secundum carnem, seu de his quæ carnis generositatem concernunt : quæ gloriatio modica est. Quod loquor de nobilitate nostra secundum carnem, non loquor, id est, loqui non videor, secundum Deum, id est sapienter et juste, quia speciem stultitiæ habet laudare se ipsum, sed quasi in insipientia, id est per modum vanitatis atque stultitiæ loquor, secundum apparentiam superficialem, quando finis interior non pensatur. In hac substantia, id est exsistentia seu materia, gloriæ hujus.
paras.en: [[11:16|I say again|Iterum dico]] what I said above, namely, *bear with me*, and *would to God you could bear with some little of my folly*; [[11:16|Let no man think me to be foolish|ne quis me putet insipientem esse]], while I glory of the spiritual graces conferred on me, since I glory not vainly but in the Lord, for the edification of my neighbours. [[11:16|otherwise|alioquin]], that is, if you do not bear with me glorying in spiritual things, [[11:16|take me as one foolish|velut insipientem accipite me]] glorying in carnal things, in the manner to be spoken of: which glorying seems more foolish than that concerning spiritual things, although neither of them in me was vain and foolish, but undertaken for an effective cause. So then take me, [[11:16|that I also may glory a little|ut et ego modicum quid glorier]] according to the flesh, or of the things that concern nobility of the flesh: which glorying is a small thing. [[11:17|That which I speak|quod loquor]] of our nobility according to the flesh, [[11:17|I speak not|non loquor]], that is, I do not seem to speak, [[11:17|according to God|secundum Deum]], that is, wisely and justly, because praising oneself has the appearance of folly, [[11:17|but as it were in foolishness|sed quasi in insipientia]], that is, I speak in the manner of vanity and folly, according to surface appearance, when the inner end is not weighed. [[11:17|in this matter of glorying|in hac substantia gloriæ]], that is, in this existence or matter of this glory.

paras.t: Cur autem Apostolus voluerit secundum carnem gloriari, subjecit. Quoniam multi falsi atque pestiferi gloriantur secundum carnem, id est carnaliter, seu de his quæ carnis dignitatem respiciunt, ut sunt nobilitas generis, conditionis libertas ; et ego gloriabor de iisdem, non tamen eodem fine quo illi, sed ne a vobis æstimer illis inferior, sicque contempto me, propriæ salutis patiamini detrimentum. Gloriabor ergo hoc modo, non obstante quod videatur inane et stultum.
paras.en: Why the Apostle wished to glory according to the flesh, he adds. [[11:18|Seeing that many|Quoniam multi]] false and pestilent men [[11:18|glory according to the flesh|gloriantur secundum carnem]], that is, carnally, or of things that regard the dignity of the flesh, such as nobility of race and freedom of condition; [[11:18|I will glory also|et ego gloriabor]] of the same, yet not with the same end as they, but lest I be thought by you inferior to them, and so, despising me, you suffer loss of your own salvation. I will glory then in this way, notwithstanding that it seems vain and foolish.

paras.t: Libenter enim suffertis insipientes, quum sitis ipsi sapientes. Locus iste dupliciter explanatur. Primo sic : Libenter, id est caritative ac prompte, sine omni murmuratione, suffertis insipientes, id est homines passionatos, vitiosos, ac indoctos, æquanimiter patiendo importunitatem eorum in verbis et factis. Unde Salomon loquitur : Ne respondeas stulto secundum stultitiam suam, ne efficiaris ei similis ; et iterum alius, Non litiges cum homine linguato, nec communices homini indocto. Hos ergo libenter suffertis, quum sitis ipsi sapientes, id est virtutibus eruditi secundum Christi doctrinam. Hoc enim ad veram sapientiam pertinet, ut insipientes tolerentur, nisi eorum perversitas noceat bono communi, aut propter excessum intolerabilis fiat. Verumtamen quidam, non ex caritate et humilitate, sed ex superbia et vanitate sufferunt insipientes : quia quum aliquid ab eis patiuntur, mox reputant eos stultos ac miseros, et indignum judicant ut se tam vilibus opponant, vel eos respiciant aut affentur. Hi insipientiores sunt his quos reputant insipientes. — Porro, quod libenter sustineatis insipientes, hinc constat : Sustinetis enim lætanter pro Christi amore præmioque futuro, si quis vos in servitutem redigit, id est, suo dominio subjicit : sicut frequenter in primitiva Ecclesia infideles tyranni redegerunt fideles in servos et famulos. Sustinetis insuper si quis devorat, id est, bona vestra consumit, si quis accipit, id est, vestra rapit, vel vos ipsos comprehendit : quemadmodum de quibusdam Dominus apud Prophetam protestatur, Comederunt carnem populi mei, et pellem desuper excoriaverunt ; si quis extollitur, id est, vobis se præfert, vel superba verba contra vos profert ; si quis in faciem vos cædit alapas dando : impletis enim illud in Evangelio, Si quis te percusserit in unam maxillam, præbe ei et alteram. Secundum ignobilitatem dico vos hæc sustinere, id est, hæc tanta sustinetis, tanquam ignobiliores injuriatoribus vestris, de carnis nobilitate lætantibus, quasi nos infirmi fuerimus in hac parte, id est, sic ista sustinetis ab illis, quasi nos illis ignobiliores essemus : quod ita non est, sicut patebit.
paras.en: [[11:19|For you gladly suffer the foolish: whereas yourselves are wise|Libenter enim suffertis insipientes, cum sitis ipsi sapientes]]. This place is explained in two ways. First thus: [[11:19|gladly|Libenter]], that is, charitably and promptly, without any murmuring, [[11:19|suffer the foolish|suffertis insipientes]], that is, men ruled by passion, vicious and unlearned, bearing with equanimity their importunity in words and deeds. Hence Solomon says: [[Prov 26:4|Answer not a fool according to his folly, lest thou be made like him|Ne respondeas stulto secundum stultitiam suam, ne efficiaris ei similis]]; and again another: [[Ecclus 8:4|Strive not with a man that is full of tongue|Non litiges cum homine linguato]], [[Ecclus 8:5|Communicate not with an ignorant man|nec communices homini indocto]]. These then you gladly suffer, [[11:19|whereas yourselves are wise|cum sitis ipsi sapientes]], that is, schooled in virtues according to Christ's teaching. For it belongs to true wisdom that the foolish be tolerated, unless their perversity harm the common good or become intolerable through excess. Yet some suffer the foolish not out of charity and humility but out of pride and vanity: for when they suffer something from them, they at once account them fools and wretches, and judge it unworthy to set themselves against such vile persons, or to look at them or speak to them. These are more foolish than those they account foolish. — Further, that you gladly bear the foolish is clear from this: [[11:20|For you suffer|Sustinetis enim]] joyfully for the love of Christ and the future reward, [[11:20|if a man bring you into bondage|si quis vos in servitutem redigit]], that is, subjects you to his dominion: as often in the primitive Church infidel tyrants reduced the faithful to slaves and servants. You bear moreover [[11:20|if a man devour you|si quis devorat]], that is, consumes your goods, [[11:20|if a man take from you|si quis accipit]], that is, seizes your things, or seizes you yourselves: as the Lord protests of some in the Prophet: [[Mich 3:3|Who have eaten the flesh of my people, and have flayed their skin off them|Comederunt carnem populi mei, et pellem desuper excoriaverunt]]; [[11:20|if a man be lifted up|si quis extollitur]], that is, sets himself above you, or utters proud words against you; [[11:20|if a man strike you on the face|si quis in faciem vos cædit]], giving blows: for you fulfil that in the Gospel: [[Matt 5:39|if one strike thee on thy right cheek, turn to him also the other|Si quis te percusserit in unam maxillam, præbe ei et alteram]]. [[11:21|I seek according to dishonour|Secundum ignobilitatem dico]] [the Douay has “I seek”] that you bear these things, that is, you bear such great things as being of lower birth than those who wrong you, who rejoice in nobility of the flesh, [[11:21|as if we had been weak in this part|quasi nos infirmi fuerimus in hac parte]], that is, you so bear these things from them as if we were of lower birth than they: which is not so, as will appear.

paras.t: Secundo, et magis quidem ad litteram, exponitur sic : Libenter suffertis insipientes, id est pseudoapostolos inaniter se commendantes, quorum verba et opera suffertis, quum sitis ipsi sapientes. Ironice loquitur, ut confundantur ad pœnitentiam. Stulte quippe egerunt, sustinendo hujusmodi pestilentes. Sustinetis enim, si quis pseudoapostolus vos in servitutem redigit, id est, a libertate ac dilectione evangelicæ legis, in observantias legis scriptæ vos transfert, prædicando oportere utramque legem omnino servare, ut fallaces ; si quis illorum falsorum devorat, si quis accipit vestra : sicut de Pharisæis ait Salvator, quod devorabant domos viduarum sub obtentu prolixæ orationis ; si quis illorum extollitur contra vos, jactans se natum de semine Patriarcharum, et esse circumcisum, vos vero fuisse idololatras, et incircumcisos jam esse. Quæ autem sequuntur, exponuntur sicut jam patuit.
paras.en: Secondly, and more according to the letter, it is expounded thus: [[11:19|you gladly suffer the foolish|Libenter enim suffertis insipientes]], that is, the false apostles who vainly commend themselves, whose words and works you bear, [[11:19|whereas yourselves are wise|cum sitis ipsi sapientes]]. He speaks ironically, that they may be confounded unto penance. For they acted foolishly in bearing such pestilent men. [[11:20|For you suffer|Sustinetis enim]], [[11:20|if a man bring you into bondage|si quis vos in servitutem redigit]], some false apostle, that is, transfers you from the freedom and love of the evangelical law into the observances of the written law, preaching, as deceivers, that both laws must be kept in full; [[11:20|if a man devour you|si quis devorat]], one of those false men, [[11:20|if a man take from you|si quis accipit]] your goods: as the Saviour said of the Pharisees, that they [[Mark 12:40|devour the houses of widows under the pretence of long prayer|devorabant domos viduarum sub obtentu prolixæ orationis]]; [[11:20|if a man be lifted up|si quis extollitur]], one of them, against you, boasting that he was born of the seed of the Patriarchs and is circumcised, while you were idolaters and are still uncircumcised. What follows is expounded as already shown.

paras.t: Denique, quod falsi isti non fuerint excellentiores Apostolo, etiam in carnalibus, de quibus inaniter gloriabantur, ostenditur. In quo quis audet, id est, in quo aliquis illorum pseudoapostolorum se laudare præsumit,* audeo et ego me collaudare, non tamen eo fine quo illi (ut dictum est). Hebræi sunt lingua et natione, et ego similiter. Israelitæ sunt, id est de tribu Jacob, qui alio nomine appellatus est Israel, et ego Israelita sum. Semen Abrahæ sunt, id est, carnales, non spirituales filii Abrahæ sunt, et ego utroque modo Abrahæ filius sum. Ministri Christi sunt, secundum apparentem sanctitatem et suam præsumptionem, non autem secundum veritatem ; et ego verus Christi minister sum. Ut minus sapiens, id est per modum stultioris, dico, plus ego, id est, perfectior sum Christi minister quam illi : quod tamen dicere, videtur ad insipientiam pertinere. Ideo dico hoc ut minus sapiens, quamvis secundum veritatem, sapienter loquar et salubriter agam, ita me commendando : sicut jam dictum est sæpius.
paras.en: Finally it is shown that these false men were not more excellent than the Apostle even in carnal things, of which they vainly gloried. [[11:21|Wherein if any man dare|In quo quis audet]], that is, wherein any of those false apostles presumes to praise himself, [the margin supplies the omitted words “(I speak foolishly)”] [[11:21|I dare also|audeo et ego]] to praise myself, yet not with the same end as they (as has been said). [[11:22|They are Hebrews: so am I|Hebræi sunt, et ego]] by tongue and nation, likewise. [[11:22|They are Israelites|Israëlitæ sunt]], that is, of the stock of Jacob, who by another name was called Israel[[Gen 32:28||]][[Gen 35:10||]], [[11:22|so am I|et ego]] an Israelite. [[11:22|They are the seed of Abraham|semen Abrahæ sunt]], that is, carnal, not spiritual, sons of Abraham, [[11:22|so am I|et ego]] a son of Abraham in both ways. [[11:23|They are the ministers of Christ|Ministri Christi sunt]], according to apparent holiness and their own presumption, but not in truth; and I am a true minister of Christ. [[11:23|I speak as one less wise|ut minus sapiens dico]], that is, in the manner of one more foolish, [[11:23|I am more|plus ego]], that is, I am a more perfect minister of Christ than they: which yet to say seems to belong to folly. Therefore I say this as one less wise, although in truth I speak wisely and act salutarily in so commending myself, as has now been said many times.

paras.t: Sum ergo minister Christi plus illis : Primo, in laboribus plurimis, quia pro Christi amore et proximorum conversione plus pseudoapostolis laboravi, imo et plus veris Apostolis, juxta illud : Plus omnibus laboravi ; in carceribus abundantius, id est, frequentius et durius quam illi fui incarceratus ; in plagis, id est vulneribus flagellorum mihi inflictis, supra modum humanæ virtutis seu ultra mensuram aliorum ; in mortibus, id est gravissimis pœnis seu mortis periculis, fui frequenter. Plagas vero describit, adjungens : A Judæis obstinatis ac perfidis quinquies, id est quinque vicibus, quadragenas plagas seu percussiones, una minus, id est una percussione subtracta, accepi, id est triginta novem. Erat nempe, Deo jubente, præceptum per Moysen, ut si quis aliquid dignum plagis committeret, prosterneretur, et coram adstantibus flagellaretur, ita ut pro mensura peccati esset et modus plagarum : sic tamen ut quadragenarium numerum non excederet, ne fœde laceratus frater, ante aliorum conspectum jaceret. Ne ergo Judæi viderentur crudeles, dederunt Apostolo non quadraginta, sed triginta novem plagas. Ter virgis cæsus sum a gentilibus : sicut in Actibus Apostolorum partim describitur ; semel lapidatus sum Lycaoniæ a Judæis, quando me traxerunt extra civitatem, æstimantes me mortuum : prout in Actibus legitur ; ter naufragium feci, id est sustinui ; nocte et die in profundo maris, id est in alto aquarum multarum, fui tempestate detentus ; in itineribus pro Christo fui sæpe, in quibus tamen sunt multæ insidiæ. Multa enim spatia perambulavit Apostolus, disseminando verbum Dei.
paras.en: I am then a minister of Christ more than they: first, [[11:23|in many more labours|in laboribus plurimis]], because for the love of Christ and the conversion of my neighbours I laboured more than the false apostles, yes, and more than the true Apostles, according to that: [[1 Cor 15:10|I have laboured more abundantly than all they|Plus omnibus laboravi]]; [[11:23|in prisons more frequently|in carceribus abundantius]], that is, I was imprisoned more often and more harshly than they; [[11:23|in stripes above measure|in plagis supra modum]], that is, in the wounds of scourges inflicted on me, beyond the measure of human strength or beyond the measure of others; [[11:23|in deaths often|in mortibus frequenter]], that is, I was in most grievous pains or dangers of death. He describes the stripes, adding: [[11:24|Of the Jews five times|A Judæis quinquies]], obstinate and faithless, that is, five times, [[11:24|did I receive forty stripes save one|quadragenas, una minus, accepi]], strokes or blows, one stroke being withdrawn, that is, thirty-nine. For there was a precept through Moses at God's command, that if anyone committed something worthy of stripes, he should be laid down and scourged before the bystanders, so that the number of stripes should be according to the measure of the sin: yet so that it should not exceed the number forty, lest the brother, foully torn, should lie before the eyes of others[[Deut 25:2||]][[Deut 25:3||]]. Lest then the Jews seem cruel, they gave the Apostle not forty but thirty-nine stripes. [[11:25|Thrice was I beaten with rods|Ter virgis cæsus sum]] by the Gentiles, as is partly described in the Acts of the Apostles[[Acts 16:22||]]; [[11:25|once I was stoned|semel lapidatus sum]] in Lycaonia by the Jews, when they dragged me outside the city, thinking me dead, as is read in the Acts[[Acts 14:18||]]; [[11:25|thrice I suffered shipwreck|ter naufragium feci]], that is, underwent it; [[11:25|a night and a day I was in the depth of the sea|nocte et die in profundo maris fui]], that is, in the deep of many waters, I was held by the storm; [[11:26|In journeying often|in itineribus sæpe]] I was for Christ, in which there are many snares. For the Apostle travelled over many lands, spreading the word of God.

paras.t: Ostensus sum quoque servus Christi præ ceteris : periculis fluminum, periculis latronum, id est sustinendo pericula mortis in fluminibus et a latronibus ; periculis ex genere,* periculis in civitate, periculis in solitudine, id est sustinendo pericula a Judæis, de genere meo exsistentibus, pericula etiam civium contra me insurgentium, atque pericula a bestiis eremi quam perambulavi ; periculis in mari, periculis in falsis fratribus, id est sufferendo discrimina mortis, non solum ex parte maris, sicut prædixi, sed etiam ab his qui versantur et insidiantur in mari, ut sunt piratæ ; patiendo item pericula varia a simulatis fidelibus, puta hæreticis, hypocritis et dolosis. De qualibus in Jeremia dicitur : Sagitta vulnerans lingua eorum, et in ore suo pacem cum amico suo loquitur, et occulte ponit ei insidias.
paras.en: I have also been shown a servant of Christ beyond others: [[11:26|in perils of waters, in perils of robbers|periculis fluminum, periculis latronum]], that is, by enduring perils of death in rivers and from robbers; [[11:26|in perils from my own nation|periculis ex genere]], [the margin supplies the omitted words “in perils from the Gentiles”] [[11:26|in perils in the city, in perils in the wilderness|periculis in civitate, periculis in solitudine]], that is, by enduring perils from the Jews, who are of my race, perils also from citizens rising against me, and perils from the beasts of the desert which I crossed; [[11:26|in perils in the sea, in perils from false brethren|periculis in mari, periculis in falsis fratribus]], that is, by suffering dangers of death not only from the sea, as I said before, but also from those who dwell and lie in wait on the sea, such as pirates; suffering likewise various perils from feigned believers, namely heretics, hypocrites and the deceitful. Of such it is said in Jeremias: [[Jer 9:8|Their tongue is a piercing arrow, it hath spoken deceit: with his mouth one speaketh peace with his friend, and secretly he lieth in wait|Sagitta vulnerans lingua eorum, et in ore suo pacem cum amico suo loquitur, et occulte ponit ei insidias]].

paras.t: Insuper fui plus ceteris servus Christi : in labore manuum mearum, de propriis laboribus victum ac necessaria procurando, et ærumna, id est inopia seu languore ; in vigiliis multis : paucissimo enim tempore dormivit Apostolus, sed die ac nocte insistebat divinis ultra omnem facultatem humanam ; in fame et siti, in jejuniis multis, in frigore et nuditate. Omnia enim incommoda ista afflictionesque corporis patiebatur Apostolus : non quod penitus nudus incesserit, nisi forte ab aliquibus spoliatus, sed quia vestimentorum penuriam passus sit : quia etsi aliquid boni habuisset, dedisset illud egenis. Hæc itaque passus sum, præter, id est ultra, illa quæ extrinsecus sunt, id est, quæ ex parte aliorum me cruciant, instantia mea quotidiana, id est, quæ mihi assidue instant atque occurrunt ex consideratione proximorum, quibus compatior, et pro quibus sollicitor. Ideo subditur : sollicitudo omnium Ecclesiarum, quia ex fervida caritate de omnium salute sollicitor sicut de propria. Sollicitudo autem mentem affligit. Quis infirmatur in anima, titubando in fide vel ceteris donis gratuitis, et ego non infirmor, id est, non affligor, ejus defectibus cordialiter compatiendo, sicut perfecta requirit dilectio ? Quis scandalizatur, id est, ad ruinam peccati inducitur ex verbo vel facto alterius inordinato, et ego non uror, id est, flamma caritatis accendor in compassione illius, et desiderando reparationem ipsius ?
paras.en: Moreover I was more than others a servant of Christ: [[11:27|In labour|in labore]] of my hands, procuring food and necessaries by my own labours[[1 Cor 4:12||]][[1 Thess 2:9||]][[2 Thess 3:8||]], [[11:27|and painfulness|et ærumna]], that is, want or weariness; [[11:27|in much watchings|in vigiliis multis]]: for the Apostle slept very little, but day and night applied himself to divine things beyond all human capacity; [[11:27|in hunger and thirst, in fastings often, in cold and nakedness|in fame et siti, in jejuniis multis, in frigore et nuditate]]. For the Apostle suffered all these hardships and afflictions of body: not that he went about entirely naked, unless perhaps stripped by some, but that he suffered want of clothing: for even if he had had anything good, he would have given it to the needy. These things then I suffered, [[11:28|Besides|præter]], that is, beyond, [[11:28|those things which are without|illa quæ extrinsecus sunt]], that is, which torment me from the side of others, [[11:28|my daily instance|instantia mea quotidiana]], that is, the things which press on me and meet me constantly from consideration of my neighbours, with whom I suffer and for whom I am anxious. Therefore is added: [[11:28|the solicitude for all the churches|sollicitudo omnium ecclesiarum]], because out of fervent charity I am anxious for the salvation of all as for my own. And solicitude afflicts the mind. [[11:29|Who is weak|Quis infirmatur]] in soul, wavering in faith or other gifts of grace, [[11:29|and I am not weak?|et ego non infirmor?]] that is, am not afflicted, heartily suffering with his failings, as perfect love requires? [[11:29|Who is scandalized|quis scandalizatur]], that is, is led to the ruin of sin by another's disordered word or deed, [[11:29|and I am not on fire?|et ego non uror?]] that is, am not kindled with the flame of charity in compassion for him, and in desiring his restoration?

paras.t: Si gloriari oportet, id est, quia necesse est me gloriari de bonis mihi concessis, ad vestri informationem, ne me pseudoapostolis inferiorem putetis ; quæ infirmitatis meæ sunt, id est de his quæ mihi conveniunt ex parte passibilitatis et humilitatis meæ, gloriabor in Domino, utpute de tribulationibus quas pro Christo sustinui, non de nobilitate prosapiæ aut sublimitate potentiæ, de quibus pseudo illi apostoli se jactant.
paras.en: [[11:30|If I must needs glory|Si gloriari oportet]], that is, since it is necessary for me to glory of the goods granted me, for your instruction, lest you think me inferior to the false apostles, [[11:30|of the things that concern my infirmity|quæ infirmitatis meæ sunt]], that is, of those things which belong to me on the side of my capacity to suffer and my lowliness, [[11:30|I will glory|gloriabor]] in the Lord, for instance of the tribulations I have borne for Christ, not of nobility of lineage or loftiness of power, of which those false apostles boast.

paras.t: Consequenter tangit Apostolus quamdam, quam passus est, specialem persecutionem, de qua gloriatur in Domino. Præmittitque juramentum, ut firmius sibi credatur : loquebatur enim tardis ad credendum. Deus et Pater Domini nostri Jesu Christi, id est Pater æternus, qui est Deus Christi secundum naturam assumptam, et Pater ejus secundum naturam divinam, scit, quem nihil latet, qui est benedictus in sæcula, id est in sempiternum laudatus, quod non mentior in his quæ dixi et dicam, videlicet : Damasci præpositus gentis Aretæ regis, id est præpositus civitatis Damascenæ, videlicet gentis Aretæ regis, id est populi subjecti Aretæ regi, sub quo iste præpositus rexit Damascum. Sumit autem Apostolus urbem pro habitatoribus ejus, puta Damascum pro gente in Damasco morante, ac subdita regi Aretæ. Hic ergo præpositus custodiebat civitatem Damascenorum, id est, ad instantiam et propter munera Judæorum custodiri fecit portas Damasci ne exirem, ut me comprehenderet in civitate latentem; et per fenestram domus muro adhærentis, in sporta dimissus sum a discipulis, per murum civitatis, et sic effugi manus ejus. Hoc etiam modo Michol dimisit David, et Rahab nuntios Josue.
paras.en: Next the Apostle touches on a certain special persecution which he suffered, in which he glories in the Lord. And he puts an oath first, that he may be more firmly believed: for he was speaking to people slow to believe. [[11:31|The God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ|Deus et Pater Domini nostri Jesu Christi]], that is, the eternal Father, who is the God of Christ according to the nature assumed, and His Father according to the divine nature, [[11:31|knoweth|scit]], from whom nothing is hidden, [[11:31|who is blessed for ever|qui est benedictus in sæcula]], that is, praised for ever, [[11:31|that I lie not|quod non mentior]] in what I have said and shall say, namely: [[11:32|At Damascus, the governor of the nation under Aretas the king|Damasci præpositus gentis Aretæ regis]], that is, the governor of the city of Damascus, namely of the nation of king Aretas, that is, of the people subject to king Aretas, under whom this governor ruled Damascus. The Apostle takes the city for its inhabitants, that is, Damascus for the people living in Damascus and subject to king Aretas. This governor then [[11:32|guarded the city of the Damascenes|custodiebat civitatem Damascenorum]], that is, at the instance and for the bribes of the Jews he had the gates of Damascus guarded lest I should go out, [[11:32|to apprehend me|ut me comprehenderet]] hiding in the city; [[11:33|And through a window|et per fenestram]] of a house adjoining the wall [[11:33|in a basket was I let down|in sporta dimissus sum]] by the disciples, [[11:33|by the wall|per murum]] of the city, [[11:33|and so escaped his hands|et sic effugi manus ejus]]. In this way too Michol let David down[[1 Kings 19:11||]][[1 Kings 19:12||]], and Rahab the messengers of Josue[[Jos 2:15||]].

paras.t: Patet ergo non esse contemnendum humanum auxilium, quamdiu ordinate et congrue haberi potest, quamvis semper in Domino sit sperandum, præsertim quum et virtus humani auxilii a Deo dependeat. Debet enim homo facere quod in se est, nec ante recurrendum est ad solum Dei suffragium, nisi quum deficit humanum. Imo non debet quisquam exspectare divinum auxilium, dum habet quod agat, ne Deum tentare videatur. Sic Ezechias piissimus videns se regi Assyriorum prævalere non posse, totum se contulit ad rogandum Dominum, ut legitur in libro Regum. Nihilo minus fecit quod in se erat, imo quidquid sibi possibile fuit, obstruendo fontes, faciendoque machinas. Unde Deus, qui Paulum usque ad tertium cœlum rapuit, poterat eum aliter liberare a prædicti manu præpositi, quam per fenestram et sportam ; sed sic eum eripuit, ut instruamur non deserere humana præsidia, nec sine necessitate ad solum Dei convolare auxilium. Hanc persecutionem est in Damasco passus Paulus, statim post sui conversionem, ut patet in Actibus Apostolorum.
paras.en: It is clear then that human help is not to be despised, so long as it can be had in an orderly and fitting way, although hope must always be placed in the Lord, especially since the very power of human help depends on God. For a man ought to do what is in him, and one must not have recourse to God's aid alone until the human fails. Indeed no one ought to wait for divine help while he has something he can do, lest he seem to tempt God. Thus the most pious Ezechias, seeing he could not prevail against the king of the Assyrians, gave himself wholly to praying the Lord, as is read in the book of Kings[[4 Kings 19:14||]]. Nonetheless he did what was in him, indeed whatever was possible to him, stopping up the springs and making engines of war[[2 Par 32:2||]]. Hence God, who caught Paul up to the third heaven[[2 Cor 12:2||]], could have delivered him from the hand of the said governor otherwise than by a window and a basket; but He rescued him thus so that we might be taught not to abandon human safeguards, nor without necessity to fly to God's help alone. This persecution Paul suffered in Damascus immediately after his conversion, as appears in the Acts of the Apostles[[Acts 9:23||]][[Acts 9:24||]][[Acts 9:25||]].
